slides.title: What you say versus what [they conclude].
slides.lede: Brand identity is the meaning you deliberately create. Brand image is the meaning people actually take away.

slides.title: One you [manage], one you only influence

cards.label: Identity
cards.text: Internal strategic decisions about your intended future position.

cards.label: Image
cards.text: Audience conclusions shaped by past and current evidence.

slides.quote: A brand is not only what an organisation publishes.
slides.text: It is also the conclusion people reach after they compare its claims with its conduct.

slides.title: Four [failure points] behind the gap
slides.note: A redesign can help recognition. **It will not solve an experience failure.**

items.title: Observed behaviour
items.text: Referrals, repeat business, conversion, complaints, pricing objections.

items.title: Direct stated perception
items.text: Interviews, surveys, win and loss conversations.

items.title: Internal interpretation
items.text: Leadership assumptions: hypotheses until externally confirmed.

slides.title: A rebrand changes identity [immediately]. Image lags behind
slides.text: Perception changes when people meet repeated, credible evidence over time. Launch a stronger promise before stronger performance and the gap becomes more visible.

slides.title: Choose the right intervention, not the most visible one.
